title: Who's Who: Priya Nand
summary: Sonance telegrapher whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Priya Nand (born 1830) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a sonance telegrapher whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Nand perfected the 1870 echo relay by tuning a receiver to a selected Referent rather than maintaining an aperture at both ends. She introduced deliberate pauses between signals to expose the false repetitions caused by similarly formed nearby objects.
Commercial relay offices owe their procedures as much to her discarded messages as to her successes.

For Alderwick readers, Priya Nand stands not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
